description:
REVIEWED 2026-10-25 (TodoReview) against origin/develop 9a184b619 and fork main ea44bcc9 (30.24.0.13). PROBLEM
downstream/patches.json in BenchBox-dev/benchbox-sqlglot records `platform-dialects`, `postgres-exact-division`, `sqlite-exact-integer-division` and `sqlite-grouping-sets` as `upstream_state: declined` with no upstream link. The blog outline (benchbox-site/drafts/building-benchbox/outlines/20-benchbox-soft-fork-sqlglot.md) says to verify 'the upstream state of the four patches recorded as declined'.

VERIFIED FACTS (2026-10-25, fork main ea44bcc9, `gh` against tobymao/sqlglot)
- The premise is wrong. downstream/MAINTAINING.md defines `declined` as 'the fork does not intend to offer it, or upstream refused it', and each of the four entries already has a non-empty `upstream_reason` stating a fork-only policy (e.g. 'Exact division is a BenchBox benchmark-correctness policy applied to every SQLite output (owner decision); upstream keeps source semantics'). No upstream PR/issue exists for these four and none is required by the contract. Only `offered` entries list upstream links.
- State counts in patches.json: 27 entries without upstream_state (original/upstreamed/excluded), 14 `not_offered`, 4 `declined`, 0 `offered`. Eleven of the 14 `not_offered` reasons already say 'a candidate' (postgres-extract-return-types, sqlite-date-interval-arithmetic, sqlite-temporal-lowering, duckdb-order-by-all-keyword, databricks-primary-key-ordering, sqlite-date-day-arithmetic, sqlite-day-offset-date, snowflake-regexp-replace-groups, empty-group-by-generator, bigquery-window-nulls-ordering, sqlite-set-operation-operands).
- Real upstream outcomes that ARE NOT recorded: issue tobymao/sqlglot#8347 'SQLite: binary DATE + INTERVAL emits SQL that SQLite cannot execute' (author joeharris76) was closed NOT_PLANNED on 2026-09-13 with no comment, yet the related SQLite date patches (`sqlite-day-offset-date`, `sqlite-date-interval-arithmetic`, ...) are `not_offered`; issue #8348 'QuestDB dialect support' was closed by the maintainer ('sorry, but we're not looking to add questdb at the moment') - it concerns original entries (`questdb-generator`, `platform-dialect-modules`), not carried ones.
- Upstream merged work: #8352 (SingleStore percentile null ordering) is authored by joeharris76; #8247, #8325 and #8440 are authored by other contributors (geooo109, fivetran-kwoodbeck, georgesittas). The outline's claims 'Four of our pull requests are already merged' and 'Upstream PRs merged: #8247, #8325, #8352, #8440' overstate authorship. patches.json attributes the three to the `qualified-star-except` (excluded) and `pushdown-projections-setop-branch-width` (upstreamed) entries as equivalent upstream changes, not BenchBox PRs.

DECISION GATES (stop and ask the owner)
G1 Vocabulary. Options: keep `declined` (recommended; the contract and tests/test_downstream_contract.py stay unchanged) and fix the blog wording to 'kept fork-only by design'; or introduce a distinct state such as `fork_only` (schema change in refresh.py/verify.py/tests; fork-maintainer decision).
G2 Recording #8347 against the SQLite date patches. Options: set those entries to `declined` with the issue URL (check the contract allows `upstream` links on `declined`; otherwise put the URL in `upstream_reason`) (recommended), or leave `not_offered` and mention the closed issue in the reason.
G3 Offering any `not_offered` candidate upstream (opening PRs or issues on tobymao/sqlglot) is an external action: owner approval per patch; this item only lists candidates.
G4 The blog edit lives in the separate benchbox-site repo: owner or Main decides whether this item edits it.

GUARDRAILS
- No new upstream PR or issue is opened here. No claim about an upstream decision without a URL that was fetched and read.
- Do not change patch contents, only metadata (`upstream_state`, `upstream_reason`, `upstream` links); a metadata-only fork PR must pass the fork's contract tests and CI; no runtime wheel bump is needed unless the fork's release rules require one (check downstream/MAINTAINING.md; if a wheel version bump is mandated, stop and ask).
- Standing rules for the fork: its own CI, no SKIP, no Co-Authored-By, identity Joe Harris.

STANDING GUARDRAILS: work only in a `make worktree-create` worktree after `make agent-write-preflight` (primary clone /Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox is read-only); run tests only through make targets (`make test-fast`, `make pr-preflight`, `make sql-execution-gate`, `make tpcds-obt-equivalence`) or targeted `uv run -- python -m pytest <paths> -n 4`; never BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_DIR, `make test-unlock` or raw broad runs; one heavy run at a time; no live-cloud spend and no production publish without explicit owner approval; published result bundles are never edited (only manifest-sidecar `known_defects` and results-data/CORPUS_NOTES.md per results-data/DEFECTIVE_DATAGEN_AUDIT.md); no SKIP / --no-verify / `git add -A`; no explanatory comments or docstrings in code (`make comment-policy-check`); uv only; identity Joe Harris, no Co-Authored-By; PR flow `make pr-preflight` once, `make pr-open`, CI + oracle review, `make pr-arm`. Stop and ask the owner on unexpected result changes, relaxed guards, oracle stand-ins or real design choices.
